# Design System: fairtrade

> **This file is the one design record for fairtrade.** It carries the visual rules and the
> component language that peasant's local web and village's frontend conform to.
>
> - **Frontmatter.** It is generated by `scripts/gen-llm-artifacts.mjs`, and CI fails if it drifts;
>   never edit it by hand.
>   - Every token value comes from `src/index.css`, the single source of token values.
>   - The script authors the rest: the typography roles (`TYPE_ROLES`), the component entries
>     (`COMPONENTS`) and the description (in `buildDesignFrontmatter`). A restyle that changes which
>     tokens a component uses must update them there.
> - **Prose.** It is authored. Where the prose quotes a value, the token wins.
> - **`llm/NEUROINCLUSIVE.md`** keeps the research behind the neuroinclusive rules stated here, one
>   line per rule naming the rule below, plus the reconciliation notes and the review checklist. A
>   rule is worded once, here. Where the two disagree, this file wins, and the disagreement is
>   a bug to fix in both files in one commit.
> - **`PRODUCT.md`** holds who the system serves.
> - **The in-use demo** (`#inuse`, fairtrade.peasantlabs.org) is the fidelity oracle. When the demo
>   and this file disagree, match the demo. Record the conflict as a numbered item on the open
>   ratification issue, add one line under "Known
>   conflicts with the demo", and put the pointer right after the conflicting clause in every
>   sentence that states it (see Status). A ratified change resolves it.
> - **Status.** A pointer, `(#<issue>/N)`, marks the clause it follows. The conflict covers what
>   the item's line under "Known conflicts with the demo" describes; there, which side changes
>   stays open until the item is decided. Everywhere else the clause binds, new fairtrade work
>   included, and so does the rest of the rule. Where a prose clause is pointed, the matching
>   frontmatter role is a known conflict too. A demo that breaks a binding rule has a defect, filed
>   on its own issue. Either way, consumers match the demo until the fix or the decision lands in
>   fairtrade first. The Overview and Key Characteristics summarize the named rules,
>   whose pointers govern. Research guidance that the library does not ship yet stays in
>   `llm/NEUROINCLUSIVE.md` until the PR that ships it adds it here.

## Overview

**Creative North Star: "styled, but functional"**

Fairtrade is one design system, for peasant (the local web app) and village (the transcript
commons), built around one job: reading an AI coding agent's trace faithfully. Craft serves use.
Every visual choice earns its place by improving legibility, orientation or speed, never decoration
for its own sake; when in doubt, remove it. The identity is a calm terminal register: a fixed-width
face for chrome, square edges, a near-black dark theme and a warm paper light theme, a desaturated
earthy palette, and one scarce amber accent. Brand character lives in precise details (the amber
active marker, the mono chrome, real provider marks), not in ornament.

The product is data-heavy (long transcripts, tables, code, dashboards), and its readers include
people who are dyslexic, have ADHD or are autistic. So the system is **neuroinclusive by default**,
not through an accessibility toggle: a 16px text floor, 1.5 prose leading, a capped prose measure,
functional borders at 3:1, a global focus ring, static-first motion, one primary action and at most
five first-class actions per view, progressive disclosure, persistent orientation and tabular numbers are baked into the tokens
and the base layer, and they govern every component.

Seven principles, in priority order:

1. **Styled, but functional.** Craft serves use.
2. **The user always knows where they are.** A sticky top nav, sticky section and conversation
   headers, and an origin-aware breadcrumb are always present. Going back restores scroll and state.
3. **Tools stay on screen.** Action bars, rails and toolbars for the current surface stay visible
   on scroll. Reaching a tool never requires hunting.
4. **Everything is aligned, and left-aligned.** One vertical axis; labels, values and content share
   a left edge; everything sits on the 4/8 grid.
5. **Glanceable.** Providers lead with real brand marks; tools and states use functional icons.
   Navigation is text-first: section links, tabs and breadcrumbs need no decorative glyph.
6. **Readable first.** Calm contrast, comfortable leading, nothing readable below 16px. Monospace is
   reserved for code and chrome.
7. **Maximize usability.** Usability beats flourish at every fork: comfortable targets, obvious
   states, minimal motion, WCAG AA in both themes.

**The Static-First Rule.** Motion is off by default (`--motion-base`). Short transitions
(`--dur-1` to `--dur-3`) belong inside `@media (prefers-reduced-motion: no-preference)`,
and the reduce block zeroes every animation and transition globally, so nothing moves under
reduce. Skeletons and live dots stay static; nothing pulses, blinks, auto-plays or auto-scrolls
the reading view. The one looping exception is the named `busy-spin` animation, only while
work is in progress and only under `prefers-reduced-motion: no-preference`;
nothing flashes more than three times a second; a live table settles at most one
change a second; the live indicator is a static filled dot. The one long entrance (`--dur-entrance`) belongs to the
presentation site's hero, never to a product surface. Press feedback is the one movement a control
makes: a button scales to 0.97 on `:active` (a chip or joined segment to 0.98), easing on
`transform` alone with `--ease-out`; `--ease-in-out` is for moving something already on screen.
Hover styles apply only under `@media (hover: hover) and (pointer: fine)`, so a tap never leaves a
control stuck in its hover state.

**Key Characteristics:**
- Two themes only, dark by default, both WCAG AA, re-themed purely by swapping tokens on `[data-theme]`.
- Square: radius 0 on every box.
- Atkinson Hyperlegible Mono for chrome, headings and code; Atkinson Hyperlegible for prose.
- All-lowercase chrome; user content keeps its case.
- Amber is the one accent and it is scarce.
- Flat: depth comes from tonal surfaces and hairlines, not shadows.
- Neuroinclusive defaults in the tokens, not behind a setting.

## Colors

A calm, desaturated earth palette on a near-black or warm-paper ground, with one amber accent;
vivid reads as cheap. Every value is a token in `src/index.css`; the frontmatter mirrors it, dark
first, with the light value under a `-light` key where it differs.

### Primary
- **Amber** (`--amber`): the single accent. The active nav marker, the active tab underline, the
  selected-row marker, links, keywords and the focus ring in the dark theme.
  `--amber-bright` is its hover state and `--amber-dim` its quiet edge (focused input border, the
  `>` of the active nav marker). The primary action is filled with the golden `--amber-fill` and
  labelled in near-black `--amber-fill-ink` in both themes; `--amber-fill-hover` is its hover fill.
  Likewise, checked inputs and selected interactive toggles use `--amber-fill` with `--amber-fill-ink`, with non-color state cues.
  A switch is the exception: on is the inverted neutral (an `--ink-strong` track, a `--canvas`
  thumb) and never amber, because a settings page holds many switches and amber stays scarce. The
  track's fill and the thumb's side carry the state, so switches show no redundant on/off word beside them. The accessible state remains `aria-checked`.
  The fill tokens are split from `--amber` so light-theme text can stay dark enough for AA. `--on-amber` is the
  ink on the remaining `--amber` fills (the current step, the current page number).

### Secondary
- **Teal** (`--teal`): the user role and informational accents (the user turn rail and label).
- **Olive** (`--olive`): success and additions; the live dot.
- **Clay** (`--clay`): danger and deletions; the danger button text.
- **Mauve** (`--mauve`): sub-agent turns. System turns use neutral `--ink-3`.
  Assistant turns take their provider's accent; user turns stay teal.

These four are the tile and chart accents (`--chart-1` to `--chart-4`). The semantic aliases map
onto them: `--success` (olive), `--warning` (amber), `--danger` (clay), each with a `-fg` ink for a
filled chip and a `-soft` tint for a background. Diffs use `--add-*` and `--del-*` (background,
text, rail).

### Neutral
- **Canvas** (`--canvas`): the page ground. Deep neutral-warm near-black in dark; warm paper in light.
- **Surfaces** (`--surface`, `--surface-2`, `--surface-elev`, `--surface-hover`): panels, selected
  rows and inset wells, overlays and hover. `--surface` equals `--canvas` in both themes: one flat
  ground, so a panel is told apart by its `--rule-strong` edge, never by a near-black grey on black.
  `--surface-2` is kept for selected rows and inset wells. `--surface-elev`, the fill of everything
  that floats (menus, a select's option list, popovers, tooltips, toasts), equals the ground too:
  a floating panel is told apart by its `--rule-strong` edge and, in the dark theme, the overlay
  lift, never by a grey or beige slab.
- **Inks** (`--ink-strong`, `--ink`, `--ink-2`, `--ink-3`, `--ink-4`, `--ink-5`): short emphasis,
  primary text, secondary, tertiary, the faintest text-safe ink, and decoration only.
- **Rules** (`--rule`, `--rule-strong`): the structural hairline divider and the functional control
  border.

### Named Rules
**The Scarce Amber Rule.** Amber marks at most one focal point per region: the primary
action, the active marker, a link, the focus ring. Small interactive controls also use amber to mark their on/selected state, paired with a tick, thumb position or label. Large fills stay low-chroma earth; amber is never small body
text on light and never a large saturated panel. Never combine color emphasis, bold and motion on one
element.

**The Text-Safe Ink Rule.** Text clears 4.5:1, and primary body text aims for 7:1. Every text ink,
`--ink-3` and `--ink-4` included, holds 6.3:1 on the ground, so muted text never reads faint. `--ink-4` is the
faintest ink that may carry text. `--ink-5` and `--rule` are decoration and structure only. `--ink-3`
is for secondary text, never primary body.

**The Functional Border Rule.** Anything that identifies a control or its state (input outlines,
button borders, toggles, focus rings, meaningful icons, chart series) clears 3:1 against every
surface in both themes: use `--rule-strong` or stronger. On the ground, `--rule-strong` holds 4:1,
so panel edges, inputs and buttons read clearly. Hairline dividers between same-tone
surfaces (`--rule`) stay deliberately subtle at 1.5:1 or higher on the ground; they structure
content without competing with controls. `scripts/contrast.mjs`, run by `pnpm build`, fails on control borders, the focus ring,
these two floors and the 6.3:1 muted-ink floor, and only reports the toggle fill, the `--amber-dim`
focus tint and the dividers on raised surfaces; icons and chart series are checked in review.

**The Never Color Alone Rule.** Status, diff, log level, role and required fields always pair color
with an icon, a text label or a shape. Negative numbers carry a leading minus.

**The Warm Paper Rule.** The light theme is warm paper, not `#fff`, and the dark theme is off-white
on near-black, not `#fff` on `#000`. Both choices remove glare and halation; do not "fix" either to
pure black or white.

## Typography

**Display Font:** Atkinson Hyperlegible Mono (with ui-monospace, Menlo, Consolas, monospace)
**Body Font:** Atkinson Hyperlegible (with ui-sans-serif, system-ui, sans-serif)
**Label/Mono Font:** Atkinson Hyperlegible Mono, the same face as display (`--font-mono`)

**Character:** One superfamily from the Braille Institute, chosen for disambiguated glyphs. The
fixed-width cut carries the terminal identity in chrome, headings and code; the proportional cut
carries everything a person reads at length.

Both faces load from Google Fonts with a `<link>` in the document head (with `preconnect`), never a
remote `@import` in app CSS. The exported `fonts.css` is deprecated for apps and retained only
for non-app compatibility; apps must use the head links. Weights: proportional 400 and 700 with italics; mono 400, 500, 600, 700
and italic 400.

### Hierarchy
- **Display** (700, `--fs-display`, `--lh-tight`): the presentation site's brand moments only.
- **Headline** (700, `--fs-xl`, `--lh-tight`): page titles.
- **Title** (700, `--fs-lg`, `--lh-tight`): section and card titles. Headings are at least 20%
  larger than body text, with at least 2em above them and more space above than below
  and a hairline under section headers. Compact toolbar labels are not headings and are demoted
  to non-heading elements. Tight leading is for single-line headings; any
  text that wraps gets at least 1.4.
- **Body** (400, `--fs-body`, `--lh-body`, `--tracking-prose` and `--word-spacing-prose`): prose,
  descriptions and transcript speech. Paragraphs are separated by at least one line-height. The measure is `--measure-prose`,
  and transcript reading panes use `--measure-read`: about 45 to 66 characters a line, never beyond
  about 80. The tokens are probe-verified in the body face with prose tracking and word spacing;
  their nominal `ch` values are not character-count guarantees. Text is left-aligned in a single column and never justified.
- **Label** (400 to 600, `--fs-label`, mono, letter-spacing 0): chrome. Nav, buttons, chips, tabs,
  table headers, metadata labels.
- **Code** (400, `--fs-body`, mono, `--lh-mono`, letter-spacing 0): code, logs, IDs and tool output
  each in its own horizontal scroller, never capped by the prose measure.

**Ledger reading-pane exception (owner ruling).** The ledger presentation derives its
reading column from the reader-width control (`--txn-reader-width`: any width from 600 CSS
pixels to the stream's whole content width, up to the lane that holds the zen control, with no
snaps) rather than a fixed `ch` cap, so prose follows the width the reader chose. Tables, code, diffs and
tool output keep their own measures and horizontal scrollers. This is the one documented exception
to the reading-measure paragraph above; every classic surface keeps `--measure-prose` and
`--measure-read`.

The presentation site also uses a locked three-tier heading ladder (`--fs-group`, `--fs-section`,
`--fs-sub`) that does not drift down the page.

Small filter captions, repository-owner labels, usage-scope labels and publish-section labels
are paragraphs, not headings. Transcript phases are level-three headings; each turn is a named
article with a level-four heading, preserving its compact visible role label. Code, tables,
metadata and the trace stream are keyboard-focusable scrollers. Technical help uses focus/tap
triggers rather than hover-only titles. Tabs name and control their mounted panel. Graph tree
items own selection/disclosure semantics; redundant pointer affordances stay out of the
accessibility tree. Native pressed/expanded/checked state is not echoed by per-control live
regions. Map focus and folder changes share one status region; settings views can use
`SettingStatus` to share save announcements while standalone `SettingRow` retains its own.

### Named Rules
**The 16px Floor Rule.** Nothing a person reads drops below 16px (`--fs-min`): table cells, code,
log lines, tooltips and data values included. Chrome labels are mono 14 (`--fs-label`).
`--fs-micro` is retired; no smaller-type exception exists. Gain density
through row height and padding, never smaller glyphs.

**The Mono Is Chrome Rule.** Mono is for code, IDs, timecodes, tabular data and chrome. Paragraphs
and transcript speech are never set in mono. Prose gets tracking, word spacing, 1.5 leading and a
capped measure; mono gets letter-spacing 0 so columns stay aligned.

**The Lowercase Chrome Rule.** UI chrome is all lowercase (nav, labels, buttons, headings, tabs,
table headers). User content is never lowercased: names, transcript text, collective names, code,
hashes and data values keep their case. Multi-line literal copy (error bodies, help, tooltips) may
use sentence case so sentences stay parseable. Never `text-transform: uppercase` on multi-word text.

**The Tabular Numbers Rule.** Every count, duration, stat and numeric column uses tabular lining
figures (`font-variant-numeric: tabular-nums`). Numeric columns right-align; plain mixed-precision
DataTable columns can align on the decimal separator without changing the values' precision.

**The One Number Format Rule.** Every number on screen goes through `src/ui/format.js` (exported
from `/ui`): compact counts read "999", "1.2k", "66.7M", "66.7B" (one decimal at most, k lowercase);
exact integers are grouped ("272,000"); costs read in dollars at cents ("$0.30"), and a positive
cost under a cent reads "<$0.01"; a missing or unreadable value reads "—". Durations and dates have
their own one format in `src/ui/transcript/time.js`. Rounding happens only for display: recorded
values, such as a harness's cost string, are kept and summed exactly.

**The Bold, Not Italic Rule.** Emphasis is weight: `em` and `i` render at 600, upright. Underline is
reserved for links. In prose, links carry a dotted underline (solid on hover and focus) so they
never rely on color alone; chrome links stay clean. A faint amber text glow belongs only to
single accent words explicitly marked `.hl` in the dark theme, never to generic bold spans or multi-line text.

## Layout

Desktop-first, left-aligned, on a 4/8 grid. The spacing scale is `--sp-1` to `--sp-8` (4, 8, 12, 16,
24, 32, 40, 56) and every padding, margin and gap uses it. The presentation site's content columns
cap at `--maxw` with `--gutter` sides. An app page does not: `AppPage` (and the in-use demo's
`.iu-page`) takes the full width of the column beside the sidebar with the same padding on the left
and the right (32px from 768px up, 16px below), so the gap beside the sidebar always equals the gap
at the window's edge; prose keeps its own measure inside it. Every page frame (the analytics
overview included) carries that inset once, and the demo's view adds none around it. Buttons and inputs share one height (`--control-h`, `--control-h-sm` for small).
Row heights come in three density tokens (`--row-h-compact`, `--row-h-standard`,
`--row-h-comfortable`).

Breakpoints are one scale (`--bp-sm`, `--bp-md`, `--bp-lg`, `--bp-xl`): phone below 480, large phone
480 to 767, tablet 768 to 1023, laptop 1024 to 1439, desktop from 1440. Desktop is the canonical
layout and narrower widths adapt down with single-sided width conditions using the four scale values
(for example, `(width < 768px)` for large phone and below); any condition that cannot use a scale
value is a recorded exception in the breakpoint fixture. Mobile complements desktop: it stays
overflow-free, legible and tappable from 320px up (WCAG 1.4.10 reflow at 400% zoom), and the desktop
layout is never compromised to serve it. Each table and code block gets its own `overflow-x: auto`.

Stacking uses one named scale: `--z-sticky` < `--z-nav` < `--z-dropdown` < `--z-dialog` < `--z-toast`
< `--z-tooltip`. `scroll-padding-top: var(--nav-h)` keeps focused and anchored content clear of the
sticky nav.

**The Five Actions Rule.** A view has one primary action and at most five first-class actions; the
rest go under an overflow menu. Table rows default to one kebab, not a row of buttons.

**The Orientation Rule.** Every surface answers where am I, what is this and how did I get here: a
stable breadcrumb, a sticky context header naming the current transcript or dataset, a definite
active nav state, position indicators in long flows ("turn 312 of 1,840"), and anchor-linkable rows.

**The Progressive Disclosure Rule.** Transcript turns start expanded and remain collapsible;
tool details start collapsed. Headline metrics expose drill-down details. The transcript's
tool-type filter subgroup starts collapsed and persists the user's disclosure choice.
Calm by default; the user opts into density.

**The Target Rule.** Every interactive box is at least 24 by 24 (`--target-min`); dense controls
may instead meet the WCAG 2.5.8 spacing exception. Primary publish actions use 36px on desktop
(`--control-h`) and 44px for coarse pointers (`--target-comfortable`); the header publish action
also uses the desktop control height, never the 28px small-control height. The glyph stays at icon size; the box is what grows.
On a coarse pointer every control reaches 44px: `--control-h` and `--control-h-sm` both rise to
`--target-comfortable`, so a control drawn at either height grows with no rule of its own, and a
fine pointer keeps 36px and 28px. A visual that must stay small (a switch track, a chip, a tag, a
badge) is drawn at `--chip-h`, which holds; when it is a control (a switch, a chip button) it takes an
invisible 44px hit box instead, as do crumb links and table sort headers.

**The Text Spacing Rule.** A user stylesheet with WCAG 1.4.12 spacing (line-height 1.5, paragraph
spacing 2x, letter 0.12em, word 0.16em) clips nothing: no fixed px heights on text containers, and
message content never truncates. Primary labels and titles wrap; paths and prompt previews
may ellipsize only with their complete text available through a title or detail view.

**The Help In Place Rule.** Help at the point of use (column headers, metrics, jargon) opens on
hover and on keyboard focus (`Tooltip`, `Term`), and `Term` also opens on tap.

**The Same Place Rule.** The same controls sit in the same place on every view, and identical
actions carry identical labels and icons. Nothing reflows, reorders or submits without an explicit
action.

## Elevation & Depth

Flat by default. The page and its panels share one ground (`--surface` equals `--canvas`); depth
comes from edges first (hairline and functional borders, `--bd` and `--bd-strong`), then from
`--surface-2` for selected rows and inset wells, not from shadows. Overlays fill with
`--surface-elev`, which is the same ground, so they are told apart by their strong edge and the
overlay lift, not by a fill. Every region with running text or data sits on one flat fill: no gradients, patterns,
scanlines or textures behind reading content. Overlays, sticky headers and command palettes use
opaque surfaces.

### Shadow Vocabulary
- **Amber glow** (`--glow`, `--glow-soft`): a faint text glow only on accent words (`.hl`),
  and a faint halo on floating panels and the selected graph node. Dark
  theme only: the light theme sets both to `none`.
- **Overlay lift**: in the dark theme, dialogs, floating menus and popovers separate from the page
  with the one `--overlay-shadow` token; the light theme sets it to `none`.
- **Selection inset**: an inset `--stroke-emphasis` (2px) amber bar
  marks the active turn, outline item or palette row without shifting layout.

### Named Rules
**The Opaque Chrome Rule.** No glass or blur in the base UI. Any `backdrop-filter` sits behind
`prefers-reduced-transparency: no-preference` with an opaque fallback. Under
`prefers-reduced-transparency: reduce`, nothing blurs and the sticky chrome is opaque.

**The Texture Stays Out Rule.** ASCII texture lives on non-text chrome and display surfaces only
(hero art, thumbnails, empty states), never behind prose or data. Glow follows the Shadow
Vocabulary above.

## Shapes

Square and editorial. Radius is 0 on every box: cards, controls, chips, tags, inputs, dialogs,
menus, tooltips, graph nodes. The only curves are true circles whose shape is the meaning: status
dots, radio marks and busy spinners. Borders are 1px (`--stroke-hairline`); 2px
(`--stroke-emphasis`) is reserved for active and selected emphasis such as the tab underline and
role rails. The focus ring uses `--focus-ring-width` (3px) and `--focus-ring-offset` (2px).
The one inset variant uses `--focus-ring-offset-inset` (-3px), only where an outside ring
would be clipped or collide with a neighbour; it keeps the same width and color.

## Components

The component library is `src/ui` (imported from the `src/ui` barrel), one family per file with a
colocated story and an entry in the generated `public/components.json`. Components emit namespaced,
token-styled classes; the styling lives in `src/index.css` and the per-component CSS files. The
presentation page (`src/sections-react`, `src/App.jsx`) and the in-use demo (`src/mockups/inuse`)
render the same system.

### Buttons
- **Shape:** square (radius 0), one height per size (`--control-h`, or `--control-h-sm` for small),
  mono label chrome, lowercase.
- **Primary:** `--amber-fill` with `--amber-fill-ink` at weight 600; hover moves to
  `--amber-fill-hover`. One per view.
- **Press and hover:** every button scales to 0.97 on press under
  `prefers-reduced-motion: no-preference`; hover styles apply only to a fine hovering pointer.
- **Secondary:** transparent with a `--rule-strong` border and `--ink` text; hover tints the text
  `--amber-bright` and the border `--amber-dim`.
- **Ghost:** transparent `--ink-3` text; hover raises to `--ink` on `--surface-hover`.
- **Danger:** transparent `--clay` text with a `--rule-strong` border that turns clay on hover.
  Reserved for deleting things.
- **Disabled:** reduced opacity, not-allowed cursor, no pointer events.

### Chips and tags
- **Style:** mono label on a `--rule-strong` border at the small control height; tags add a
  `--surface-2` fill. A provider chip leads with its brand mark (`<Tag brand="claude">`).
- **State:** outcome states (redacted, partial, failed) always pair an icon with the word.

### Integrity flag
- **Badge:** drawn only for a served flag, inline to the right of the transcript title on the
  title's line, one `--sp-4` (16px) after its text: one outlined button reading the warning glyph,
  the words suspicious transcript and a (?) glyph. No fill at rest, never amber-filled; the edge
  and the warning glyph are `--warning`, the words are `--ink` and the (?) glyph is `--ink-2`. It
  is the control height, so 44px on a coarse pointer.
- **Placement:** never in the header's actions row, so the host's actions (not published, publish)
  hold the same place whether or not a transcript is flagged. A title that fills its line, and
  every header narrower than 768px, wraps the badge under the title at its left edge, one `--sp-4`
  below. The badge keeps its words at every width. It sits with the title in the part of the header
  that folds away on scroll, so a condensed header does not show it; the turn marks stay.
- **Help:** the badge is the one control. Its accessible name is the help question, which contains
  the visible words, and it opens a short explanation panel (`aria-expanded`, `aria-controls`). The
  panel opens toward the side of the badge that has room and stays inside the transcript viewer and
  the viewport by the page gutter. It never opens on its own or on hover, never moves focus, and
  Escape or a press outside closes it; Escape returns focus to the badge. Folding the header away
  closes it too.
- **Wording:** every string the badge, the panel and the turn marks show lives in `INTEGRITY_COPY`
  (`src/ui/transcript/integrity.js`), the one place to edit it.
- **Turn mark:** a flagged turn carries the same glyph and the word flagged on its head, so the cue
  is a shape and a word, not a colour. A ledger action block that folds a flagged turn says so.
  Turns are marked only when the served content hash equals the hash of the rendered content;
  otherwise the badge draws alone.
- **No clean state:** a transcript without a flag draws nothing. There is no verified, clean or
  checked state, because an absent flag proves nothing.

### Cards / Containers
- **Corner Style:** square (0).
- **Background:** `--surface` on the canvas.
- **Shadow Strategy:** none at rest (see Elevation & Depth). Cards, the library `Card` included,
  lift 2px on hover, only under `prefers-reduced-motion: no-preference`.
- **Border:** `--bd-strong`.
- **Internal Padding:** `--card-pad` (24px, 16px below 768px), the same on all four sides of a card,
  a dialog's parts, an empty state and the left and right of every setting row and group summary,
  with `--sp-3` gaps. A row's label starts at the left padding and its control group ends at the
  right padding; nothing touches a border. Setting rows keep a `--row-h-comfortable` minimum height
  and centre their content; stacked on a phone, the control group takes its own line and still ends
  at the right padding. `scripts/journey/card-insets.journey.mjs` measures it on the demo's settings
  screens and fails on a breach.

### Inputs / Fields
- **Style:** `--canvas` fill, `--rule-strong` border, the body face at 16px without prose tracking,
  the control height.
- **Focus:** the border shifts to `--amber-dim` and the global 3px focus ring appears on keyboard focus.
- **Native parts:** the browser's own parts follow the theme (`color-scheme`), so a native select's
  option list, scrollbars and pickers are drawn dark on the dark ground and light on paper; where
  the browser lets a page style the option list, it takes the overlay fill and the inks.
- **Error / Disabled:** errors are field-adjacent, persistent and plain-language, never a transient
  toast. Checkboxes and radios are real inputs, so focus, disabled and checked states are native.

### Navigation
- **Top nav:** fixed and sticky with the brand stalk, mono 14 lowercase links in `--ink-3`, the
  active link in amber led by the one permitted `>` marker (in `--amber-dim`), a search affordance
  (cmd-k), the storybook link and the theme toggle. Selection toggles use a selected state and
  `aria-pressed`, never a decorative `>` prefix.
- **Tabs:** mono lowercase, `--ink-3` at rest, the active tab in `--ink` with a 2px amber underline;
  counts are tabular in `--ink-4`.
- **Trails:** breadcrumb, step indicator, tabs and pagination; orientation lives here.
- **App sidebar:** `AppSidebar` is the one sidebar for every app screen (online, local and docs),
  in one order that every app gets, enforced by the component so no app can drift: (1) the brand
  row, the mark with the collapse control; (2) the app's own pages (`groups`; settings is never
  one of them); (3) the shortcuts, pushed toward the footer with a hairline above them: search
  first (`search`, with a quiet mono key hint), the docs, then the app's links that leave it
  (`elsewhere`, or any `external` item, which the component lifts out of the groups);
  (4) the footer, one compact row
  pinned under the nav with a hairline above it: the account on the left (avatar or initial and
  handle, or the host's signed-out slot) at the nav icons' inset, and on the right two square icon
  buttons, the settings gear (`settingsHref`, or a `settings` item the component lifts out of the
  groups; current on the settings page) and the theme toggle (`theme` with `onThemeChange`, named
  for the theme it switches to, "switch to dark mode"), each with its tip above it and never over
  the account. A visible label carries no tooltip: tooltips belong to the collapsed rail, where
  each item shows its label, and to icon-only buttons. The phone drawer keeps the same order. The
  parts:
  the wheat mark alone (its name is the accessible name and the tooltip; the full logo with the
  wordmark belongs to the landing page only), a collapse handle seated on the column's right edge
  level with the mark (a small square whose chevron turns to point the way the column will go)
  down to an icon rail whose labels become titles, a resizable width (pointer drag, or arrow keys,
  Home and End on the separator), groups of items with an icon or a colour swatch, the current item
  marked with `aria-current` and the amber inset bar, an outside-the-app marker, the switcher to
  the docs (never the app the reader is in, and never online or local, in any app; each opens in a
  new tab unless its entry names a target). Community is hidden from menus until that surface is
  available. Brand text is `peasant`, never `peasant labs`.
  Collapse and width persist per browser. Below 768px it becomes a top bar whose menu opens the
  same nav as an opaque drawer; the menu button then becomes the drawer's one close control.
  `AppSidebarLayout` places it beside the page. Its motion runs only under
  `prefers-reduced-motion: no-preference`, on transform and opacity, and every transition can be
  interrupted: the drawer slides in from its edge over `--dur-3` and out over `--dur-2` while the
  scrim fades, its items stagger in a quarter of `--dur-1` apart, the menu glyph turns into a cross,
  an expanded rail's labels fade in from a 4px offset while the width snaps, items press to 0.98,
  and one indicator slides between current items instead of jumping.
- **Settings section bar:** `SettingsNav` lists one settings page's sections inside the page body,
  so a settings page never takes over the app sidebar; the account settings, a collective's
  settings and the local app's settings all use it. `SettingsLayout` places it beside the sections
  when the body is at least 44rem wide (a sticky column, the current section on the `--surface-2`
  fill with the amber inset bar and an amber icon) and above them when narrower (one row that
  scrolls sideways, the current section underlined in amber like a tab, kept in view). A section is
  a route link, an in-page anchor or a button, marked with `aria-current` (`page`, `location` or
  `true`); on one long page of anchors, `spy` marks the section being read.
- **In-use shell:** the app switcher replaces the page header at the same height and carries a
  keyboard tablist for the three apps.
- **Local app sections:** `LOCAL_APP_SECTIONS` in `src/ui/inuse/InUseShell.jsx` is the canonical
  registry and the list of record. An entry marked `inNav: false` keeps its id, label and route and
  is reached by route only; every other entry sits in the section nav. A consumer derives its nav and
  routes from the registry and fails loudly on an id it does not map. `GRAPH_APP_SECTIONS` is a
  deprecated alias kept for consumers on the older three-section shape.
  Main navigation is home, settings. The online page is reached by route only; it is labelled
  `online` and keeps the id and route `village`. Online presents saved relevant collective
  observations and separately pageable contribution evidence, with independently dated fetch
  results. Hosts own network operations and authorization; observations never grant permission.

### Transcript viewer (signature component)
The reading view both apps embed (`TranscriptViewer`, fed only by `adaptTranscript`). A header whose
title and meta chips leave once the trace scrolls while its breadcrumb and actions row stays pinned,
with the tab strip, the condensed scrubber header (provider, model, position) and the turns bar.
Role-accented turns, each led by an icon: user in teal, assistant in its provider's accent,
sub-agents in mauve, system in `--ink-3`. Collapsible tool-call rows with tool icons, thinking blocks, unified diffs (rail, gutter,
sign) and code blocks. Syntax highlighting renders structured output only
(`codeToHast` or `codeToTokens` through React); raw highlighter HTML is never injected. Token
evidence is disclosed by owner and scope. Recorded costs stay strings, labeled as harness estimates,
not billing. Structured native details stay outside conversation counts and search. The Pi fixture
shows this at `?app=transcript&transcript=pi#inuse`.

### Canvas and graph
The map and graph surface: a dot-grid background, square nodes (intensity fill, selected in amber),
orthogonal structure edges with dashed activity edges, persistent zoom controls, a minimap and an
activity time strip.

### Dialogs and overlays
A scrim over a bordered `--surface` card with header, body and footer; the primary action sits
bottom-right. User-opened modals, including publish, trap focus under the APG dialog pattern
and restore focus to the opener on close. Routine messages go
to one polite live region, never a focus-stealing toast. Destructive actions confirm or undo.

### Forms and empty states
The filter sidebar, form fields with functional labels, and the empty state: an icon ring, a
title, a body and one action. Every settings section is the same card (`SettingGroup`), and every
setting row is one grid: the left column holds the label and at most one help line on one left edge;
the right column holds the value or control, ending at the right padding. A long value (a
description) stacks under its label at the same left edge, never in a column of its own, and a
divider spans the card's inner width. No free sentence sits between rows: a note that matters
becomes a row. The save status sits before the control and takes no room while idle, so "saving"
and "saved" grow leftward and the control never moves. On a phone a row stays on one line where
it fits; a select drops to its own line at the right padding. The card inset gate checks all of it.
No provenance chip ("not in peasant config", "this computer only") sits on a setting.

### Data tables and charts
The data families are the data table, pagination, accordion, timeline, toast and date range.

- **Tables** (TanStack-backed `DataTable`): hairline rows with full-row hover, a header with a rule
  under it at weight 600 (to compensate for lowercase), sortable columns with an explicit sort arrow,
  and a selection that pairs an amber tint with a non-color marker. Zebra striping only past five
  columns or fifteen rows. Columns are ordered by importance, and each header matches its column's
  alignment (numeric alignment is in the tabular numbers rule).
- **DataTable defaults:** all supplied rows render without injected search, column filters,
  pagination, or a vertical height cap. The first identifier column stays frozen on horizontal
  scroll (beside the selection column when present). Rows use `--row-h-standard` (40px), expand
  for wrapping content and keep readable 16px data. An explicit `maxHeight` creates a bounded
  keyboard-scrollable region with a sticky header; natural height is the default.
- **Optional table controls:** the `toolbar` render callback can compose `DataTableToolbar` with
  its search binding, column-filter binding, or both, plus importer-owned actions. Active opted-in
  filters have a text indicator and individually removable chips. Explicit `pagination` or
  `defaultPagination` settings enable paging and its default footer. A `footer` render callback
  can compose `DataTablePaginationControls` or host-owned content. Its count reports visible rows
  and the filtered total, or the host total with `rowCount` and no active filter. With an active
  filter on a partial host window it reports `showing X of Y loaded`, never a global match total.
- **DataTable state:** sort and selection retain their existing controlled/uncontrolled props.
  Search, column filters and pagination each accept a controlled value, default seed and value
  callback. User search/filter changes reset the page to zero. With `rowCount`, pagination stays
  manual: the host supplies its window and total, which sets the page count. Search and column
  filters still apply locally to the given rows, and sorting stays local. While a filter is active
  on a partial window the count reports `showing X of Y loaded`, never the host total; clearing
  the filter restores the host-total count. With a fully loaded window the count keeps the host
  total in both states.
  The host alone maps state to URL parameters. DataTable never reads or writes routing or storage,
  fetches data, or requires a provider.
  A cumulative load-more host can keep its existing controls and leave table pagination off;
  supplied parent and child rows are not paginated again. Hosts remove their duplicate count
  only when explicitly adopting the table footer. Page-based hosts provide `pagination` and
  `onPaginationChange` and supply the requested slice.
- **Decimal columns:** `align: 'decimal'` aligns decimal separators for plain dot-separated numeric
  values by reserving the visible column's largest fractional width, with tabular figures. Integers
  reserve an invisible separator; values keep their precision. Custom renderers, currency and
  locale-formatted strings use the right-aligned tabular fallback. Headers match the right edge.
- **Long content** is chunked into labelled segments with stable fragments.
- **Charts** (Recharts wrapped, never raw): square bars and lines, token series colors, a muted
  hairline grid (never amber), mono tabular ticks, direct or swatch-and-label legends, keyboard
  access and static-first rendering.

### Icons and brand marks
- **Functional icons** are Lucide only (`lucide-react`), one stroke family at `--ic-sm`, `--ic-md`
  or `--ic-lg`. Tools, states and roles use functional icons; navigation is text-first.
  Company/provider identities, including the `github` account row, always lead with a real brand mark.
- **Brand marks:** when the UI names a company or provider, it leads with that provider's real mark
  (`<BrandMark name="claude" />`; aliases resolve anthropic to claude, google to gemini, codex to
  openai), never a generic stand-in. Marks are single-color via `currentColor`, sized off the icon
  tokens, undistorted and paired with the provider name. A mark beside its visible name is
  decorative; a mark standing alone as the identity passes `label`. Claude, Gemini, OpenAI, Cursor
  and opencode geometry originates from Simple Icons (CC0, inlined). Strike's comes unchanged from
  its official project favicon, used with the project's permission. Pi uses the official OAuth mark
  from `earendil-works/pi` (MIT) in the mauve token. The opencode mark is provisional upstream.
- **The brand stalk** (`#logo`, five paths in `src/sections-react/00-defs.jsx`) is the only inline
  brand glyph: the nav brand and the in-use banner.

### ASCII imagery (display surfaces only)
Procedural and image-filtered ASCII is a deliberate centerpiece restricted to a few low-traffic
display surfaces, rendered by `src/effects.jsx`: the wheat video hero (`AsciiVideo`), the brand
section's soil field and roots over the wordmark, the philosophy portrait field, and card
thumbnails (`AsciiImage`, whose ink follows the theme). Dense reading views stay icon-light, and
vector chrome and ASCII never mix on one element.

## Do's and Don'ts

### Do:
- **Do** reference a token for every color and size (`var(--amber)`, `var(--sp-4)`); tokens live
  in `src/index.css` and ship as `@peasant-labs/fairtrade/tokens.css`.
- **Do** keep both themes at WCAG AA and re-theme only by swapping tokens on `[data-theme]`.
- **Do** keep reading text at 16px or more and chrome at mono 14.
- **Do** write chrome in lowercase and keep user content in its own case.
- **Do** use tabular numbers on every count, duration and numeric column.
- **Do** lead every provider name with its `<BrandMark>`.
- **Do** keep 1.5 prose leading, 24px targets, the standard or sanctioned inset `:focus-visible`
  ring and a reduced-motion path for anything that moves.
- **Do** land a new visual pattern here, in the demo first, before a consuming app uses it.
- **Do** keep chrome copy plain, literal and short, with verb and object on buttons
  ("export transcript", not "ok"); errors say what happened and what to do.

### Don't:
- **Don't** hardcode a hex or px value outside the token blocks.
- **Don't** round a box corner.
- **Don't** use amber for large fills, small body text on light, chart gridlines or more than one
  focal point per region.
- **Don't** carry meaning by color alone.
- **Don't** set `outline: none` without a stronger replacement, justify text, loop an animation
  other than the named busy-spinner exception, or add motion outside `prefers-reduced-motion: no-preference`.
- **Don't** put glass, blur, gradients or texture behind reading content.
- **Don't** set prose or transcript speech in mono, or italicize for emphasis.
- **Don't** load app fonts with a remote `@import`; use the `<link>` form.
- **Don't** inject highlighter HTML; use structured Shiki output rendered through React.
- **Don't** use em dashes, middot separators or buzzwords (delve, leverage, robust,
  seamless, crucial, elevate, foster, tapestry, landscape, journey, ultimately), or "not X, but Y"
  constructions.
- **Don't** decorate chrome as a fake terminal: no `//` comment markers, no `>` prompt prefixes on
  titles, labels or bullets (the active nav marker is the one `>`), no eyebrow or kicker labels above
  a heading, no decorative captions under imagery. A presentation-site section is a title and at
  most one subtitle; an app page or section is a title alone (see the next rule).
  Bullets use a plain `-` or a small box marker in `--ink-4` or `--ink-5`. Form-field labels, control
  sub-labels and section titles are functional, not eyebrows.

- **Don't** put an explainer sentence beside or under a page or section heading in an app (online,
  local, docs chrome). App pages lead with the title and the controls; the heads lay out cleanly
  with the title alone. What may still sit under a heading is information, not a description of the
  page: a figure or a count, user content (a collective's purpose), a row's own help, or a warning
  that restates a server decision (that observations grant no permission). The in-use demo follows
  the rule, so it never reintroduces an explainer.

### Known conflicts with the demo
None currently registered. Resolved decisions and their source/record evidence are checked by
`pnpm audit:design-decisions`. A future conflict must be recorded and ratified before changing
the binding rule; do not silently promote a demo defect into policy.
